transcript:
Header:
Date: 2027-03-16 16:00 UTC
Duration: 58 minutes
Attendees: Jordan (Redwood AE), Maya (Redwood SE), Aisha (SRE Manager), Liam (Platform), Priya (ML lead), Noah (Security)

Summary:
Quick show-and-tell of Redwood Console "NeedleTrace" workflows: request-level tracing, error analysis, request logs, and debugging flows. Focus on how to correlate model outputs with infra signals, KV cache misses, and fallback routing. Customer questions on data residency, SOC2, and pilot scope.

Topics:
- Console: request inspector (needletrace) UI and timeline
- Trace stitching across retries, fallbacks, and dedicated/dynamic hosts
- Error classification and taggable playbooks
- Exporting traces and sharing with SRE/ML teams

--- Transcript ---
[00:00] Jordan: hey everyone thanks for joining, um we're gonna walk through the NeedleTrace flow in the Redwood Consol, sorry Consol — little typo — the console, uh Maya's gonna demo. If you could just say quick intros?
[00:12] Aisha: Aisha, SRE manager at HarborBridge, we run the inference infra for our legal docs product, mostly low-latency chat and some batch reranking. We're looking at request forensics today, thanks.
[00:22] Liam: Liam here, platform eng, in charge of routing and autoscaler.
[00:25] Priya: Priya, head of ML, curious how trace ties back to model versions and prompt changes.
[00:31] Noah: Noah, security, I'll ask compliance stuff later.
[00:34] Maya: Maya Chen, I'm the systems SE at Redwood. I'll take the demo, Jordan will field pricing and next-s steps.
[00:40] Jordan: cool, jumping in.

[02:05] Maya: okay opening the console, top-left is the request search bar, you can filter by trace id, request path, user id, model, or route. I'm going to search for a sample failure we ingested last week. Note: the demo data's synthetic so some names will look funky.
[03:10] Maya: here's a request detail, timeline at top shows the token timeline, then infra events, KV cache hits are green, misses are orange — the UI sometimes labels KV as K-V cash in the transcript export, we've seen that, sorry — the important part is you can see the model call, then a fallback to a smaller quantized variant.
[04:02] Aisha: can you show where I see the reason for fallback? is that explicit?
[04:08] Maya: yes, there's an event "fallback-route-trigger" with tags: latency spike, decode error, and policy=cost_saving. If you click the event, it expands the metadata including the model hash, the container host, GPU type (A10g in this demo), and the sequence length for the request.
[05:05] Liam: where does the policy come from? our autoscaler triggers or the routing tier?
[05:12] Maya: policy is from the routing layer; customers can configure rules — e.g., pin to dedicated GPUs then a fallback policy to shared hosted. We show the policy id and the evaluated rule.

[07:00] Priya: how do we correlate prompt changes to quality regressions? if we update prompt templates, can we search traces that used that prompt?
[07:12] Maya: yes, you can tag requests with prompt version metadata via SDK headers. We also have automatic signature matching: the console tries to group similar prompts via a fingerprint — it's not perfect, but it helps find regressions.
[08:00] Jordan: quick question on retention: how long are traces stored under hosted vs dedicated?
[08:10] Maya: hosted has 90 days default for traces, with long-term export to S3 or GCS for archived traces. Dedicated/private you can control retention and bring-your-own storage; we also offer a 30/90/365 slider in console for quick config.

[09:30] Aisha: our auditors will want an immutable log for a subset of requests, can we do WORM exports?
[09:38] Noah: yes and that ties to SOC2 stuff we need.
[09:42] Maya: we support append-only exports to an S3 bucket with server-side encryption; Redwood will sign the transfer and we can provide audit hashes. Jordan will send the SOC2 pack.

[11:05] Maya: moving on to error analysis view — this groups errors by signature, shows counts, p50/p95 latency, model response codes. You can open a cluster and see example payloads, and there's a quick diff UI to see before/after prompt or model version.
[12:15] Liam: example payloads — are they redacted automatically? we need PII masking.
[12:22] Maya: we provide redaction plugins; by default the console stores raw traces in the customer's org but in private deployments we run a pre-ingest redaction pipeline. For hosted, you can configure transformers to mask or hash PII before storage.

[14:40] Priya: how does KV cache miss data appear in traces? we saw an outage where many misses correlated to latency.
[14:47] Maya: each trace includes a cache layer event with hit/miss and TTL. You can aggregate by keyspace to find hot keys. There's also a heatmap view for cache churn. In our demo you can see a spike at 14:10 UTC causing a 200ms tail.
[15:50] Aisha: can we set alerts from those metrics?
[15:55] Maya: yes, alerts can be emitted to PagerDuty/Slack, and we support custom webhook templates.

[18:00] Jordan: curious about exporting and sharing traces with non-Redwood teams?
[18:07] Maya: export options: JSON, parquet, or a share link with time-limited access. Share links respect RBAC and only data the user has permission to see.
[19:00] Priya: does the trace capture the model logits or is that redacted?
[19:08] Maya: for privacy we don't surface raw logits in hosted by default; customers can opt-in for more verbose captures in private/dedicated setups. We can also hash vectors before storing.

[21:30] Speaker 1: (muffled) how many concurrent traces can we query?
[21:38] Maya: the query layer scales with dedicated capacity; for hosted we throttle heavy exports to protect tenant QoS. For large-scale forensic queries we recommend export to S3 and run analytics there with our ETL template.

[24:00] Jordan: ok let's go through a root-cause example — Maya?
[24:06] Maya: sure — opening a failure cluster, step one: look at header to get model version, route, and token counts. Step two: inspect infra events, which show a retry loop where service mesh returned 503 and the runtime retried then the request timed out leading to a fallback. The timeline shows membrane, sorry — I mean, the request queued on the GPU for an extra 120ms.
[25:40] Aisha: that queue time — is that visible per pod? can we map to host CPU pressure?
[25:48] Maya: yes we correlate with host metrics; we pull CPU/GPU utilization from our exporter and show it inline or linked. The trace links to the host's metrics time range so you can see the spike.

[28:10] Liam: our concern: if the KV cache warms slowly after deploy, will fallback cause quality regressions en masse? can we do progressive rollouts?
[28:18] Maya: yes, Rollouts in Console let you canary to a subset of traffic, and NeedleTrace flags show when a canary has higher error rates. We also have automated rollback policies if the quality metric delta exceeds a threshold.

[31:00] Priya: any built-in eval hooks? can we tie a prompt suite to alert on quality drift?
[31:06] Maya: Redwood Optimize has eval hooks; we can link a prompt suite so that if rouge/bleu like metric or custom rubric changes, the system tags traces and opens a regression alert.

[34:20] Noah: security question: where are encryption keys stored for traces in private deployment? KMS?
[34:27] Maya: for private we support customer-managed keys via KMS/HSM in your cloud account. For hosted we manage keys with envelope encryption but you can integrate your own KMS for dedicated.
[35:40] Noah: audit logging?
[35:44] Maya: every trace access is logged with user id and action, we persist logs to a separate audit store and can export to your SIEM.

[38:00] Jordan: price/ops question — what's rough request cost impact if we enable verbose traces across all traffic?
[38:08] Maya: verbose tracing adds per-request storage and small CPU overhead; ballpark 2-5% extra per token cost for hot paths. For heavy workloads we recommend sampling 1-5% and full capture for errors only.
[39:25] Liam: can sampling be dynamic? e.g., sample after an error or when latency > X?
[39:30] Maya: yes you can set adaptive sampling rules — sample more when errors spike or when p95 crosses a threshold.

[42:10] Maya: quick demo: set a rule to capture full traces for requests with p95 > 800ms and with user role internal-beta. I'll create one now — name: HB-long-tail-capture — and enable Slack alerts.
[43:05] [Maya clicks] done, rule created.

[45:00] Aisha: last thing — how long to get a pilot running? we want to try a week of focused traces and a small canary.
[45:09] Jordan: timeline depends on whether you want hosted or dedicated. For hosted it's just account + sandbox and it's immediate; dedicate requires sizing and infra lead time, 2-4 weeks. We recommend starting hosted pilot with VPC peering for audit if you need that.
[45:40] Priya: do you provide a script to replay our production traffic into the sandbox?
[45:46] Maya: yes we have a replay harness and a template. We'll include that in the quickstart.

[47:20] Noah: send SOC2 and specifics about retention + WORM export capabilities.
[47:26] Jordan: yes will do.

[49:00] Jordan: recap of next steps: Jordan sends benchmark/cost sheet and SOC2 docs; Maya provisions sandbox + replay harness; Liam provides traffic patterns; Noah lists compliance Qs; plan a security review call week of 3/22. Anything to add?
[49:18] Aisha: include sample traces from our last outage if possible — I'll share safely redacted ones.
[49:22] Liam: I'll send p95 and p99 numbers and current autoscaler config.

[51:00] Maya: quick note — on private deployments we can do direct S3 archiving to your account and also enable HSM for key wraps.

[54:00] Jordan: awesome thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the items.
[54:05] Priya: thanks, that was useful.
[54:10] Noah: thanks.

[57:00] Jordan: meeting end.
